_skill.name: lap_annotation
_skill.description: Per-label telemetry characteristics for the behavior parent labels (O, OD, PS, RM, MSP, MSR) that every saved lap segment must contain at least one of. EA remains documented as clean driving context, but it is not a substitute for the required behavior parent set in this flow. Each label declares its telemetry signature (trajectory_offset, expert_time_difference slope, brake overlap, opponent context, etc.) and the global_rules_by_session blocks prescribe the detection procedure. Source of truth for "does this range qualify as MSP / RM / O / OD / MSR / PS ... at all?" The circuit + circuit_section labels are picked by the LLM via the `get_circuit_id` / `locate_circuit_section` tools (geometry from `app/shared/circuit_sections.py`). Solo sessions are split by circuit section; sessions with opponent data emit only close overtake offence / defense engagement windows.
when_to_use: Lap excerpter assigning one parent label per circuit section.
Building the system prompt for the lap-flow planner/synthesizer.
Evaluator checks for parent-label justification against telemetry.

action_model.parent_segment: A saved lap parent segment is a group of one or more complete driving actions that together justify the behavior parent label over the final iloc range. It is not an arbitrary graph slice, a single apex moment, or one isolated label symptom.
action_model.action: An action is a coherent driver/expert maneuver over an iloc interval, evaluated through the related turning / trajectory, throttle input, and brake input for that same interval. Turning may be straight, constant, increasing, or unwinding; throttle and brake may be applied, released, modulated, held steady, or intentionally zero.
action_model.child_segment: Detailed child sub-segments may isolate a smaller action or phase for sub-labels, but the lap parent segment remains the action group that gives the parent behavior its context.

EA.name: Expert Adherence (Training)
EA.characteristics:
Player matches or cleanly outperforms the expert through the section.
  - Standard adherence: `trajectory_offset` stays within ±0.5 m of zero for the whole range, `expert_time_difference` is stable, and speed delta at sampled ilocs is small.
  - Expert-or-better clean section: EA can still apply when the player is ahead of the expert, gaining on the expert, or using a cleaner/faster line than the expert, even if `trajectory_offset` is wider/tighter than ±0.5 m. Require no off-track/cutting/instability evidence and no MSP / RM / MSR / PS gate.
  - When `expert_time_difference` exists, confirm with `find_trend_runs` and `compute_slope`. Use deterministic trend verdict fields; a positive but flat time gap only means the player is already behind, not that a new mistake happened inside this range.
  - When `expert_time_difference` is absent, do not rule out EA solely because the slope gate is unavailable. Use trajectory, speed/brake/throttle samples, segment shape, and the absence of MSP/RM/MSR/PS evidence; note that MSP/RM slope gates cannot be satisfied.
Mutually exclusive with MSP and RM.

MSP.name: Mistake (Practice)
MSP.characteristics:
Technical driving error causing time loss or instability, NOT caused by interaction with a close opponent.
  - MSP / RM boundary is decided by how the split section starts. If the section starts with the new mistake action (run wide, cut tight, braking / throttle error, instability, or first label-significant time-loss run), label the section MSP even if the driver later recovers, merges back, or the end-window loss rate weakens.
  - `expert_time_difference` must show time loss inside the range — confirm with `find_trend_runs` and require a `mistake_candidate_losing_time_here` / rising run whose `is_label_significant` field is true. A constant positive ms gap means the player is slower than expert, not that the mistake occurred here.
  - Use `compute_slope` as the whole-range summary only after localizing the rising run. If its final-window fields show `end_change_direction` flat/falling or `end_trend_change` weakening/reversing, describe that as later recovery inside the MSP segment instead of relabeling the whole section RM.
  - `trajectory_offset` exceeds the expert envelope: a spike outward
    (ran wide) or inward (cut tight). Recovery back toward zero later in
    the same section does not cancel MSP when the section began with the
    mistake action.
  - Use RM instead only when the section does not start with a new mistake and the first qualifying action is recovery / merge from an already-carried offset or prior incident.
  - In opponent-capable data, `classify_opponent_interaction(start, end)`
    does NOT return an adverse racing outcome (`failed_attack` or
    `broken_defense`). A close opponent + adverse classifier outcome ⇒ MSR.
Mutually exclusive with EA, RM, MSR. The detailed-annotation flow refines MSP sub-ranges later — attach MSP at the section level when the section starts with or is dominated by a technical error.

MSR.name: Mistake (Racing)
MSR.characteristics:
Time / position loss caused by an interaction with a close opponent inside the section.
  - Call `classify_opponent_interaction(start, end)`. Require
    `outcome` = `failed_attack` or `broken_defense`,
    `gates.MSR: true`, and `label_gates.MSR: true`. Low / weak
    confidence means inspect opponent trajectory or submit an empty label list.
  - Use `find_nearest_opponent` / `query_opponent_trajectory` only as
    supporting evidence for the primary slot and technique.
  - `expert_time_difference` typically grows across the
    interaction window.
Mutually exclusive with EA, RM, MSP. No close opponent or classifier outcome not in {failed_attack, broken_defense} ⇒ not MSR.

RM.name: Recovery & Merge
RM.characteristics:
Player recovering from a prior mistake inside this section.
  - RM / MSP boundary is decided by how the split section starts. Use RM when the section does not start with a new mistake action and the first qualifying behavior is recovery / merge from an already-carried offset, off-track state, instability, or prior incident.
  - A preceding mistake/off-track/incident explains why recovery is needed.
  - `expert_time_difference` should show recovery pressure inside the range. Strongest evidence is a `recovery_candidate_gaining_time_here` / falling run whose `is_label_significant` field is true. Also accept a rising whole-range gap when `compute_slope` reports the loss weakening, flattening, or reversing at the end (`end_trend_change` such as `weakening_at_end` or `reversing_to_falling_at_end`) and the action evidence shows recovery / merge.
  - `trajectory_offset` trends back toward zero from a non-zero or already-compromised start, with speed and throttle consistent with rejoining or accelerating back toward the expert's pace. This merge-back action is RM even if the absolute `expert_time_difference` gap is still growing across the whole range.
Do NOT use RM just because an MSP section has a later recovery phase; if the section starts with the mistake action, the whole parent segment is MSP and recovery is described in the reasoning or detailed child sub-segment. Do NOT attach when the player started clean with no carried mistake/off-line state — that's EA or an empty parent, not RM. Do NOT attach for normal pit exit; pit exit is PS / PS1. Mutually exclusive with EA and MSP.

PS.name: Pit Stop
PS.characteristics:
Player entering, sitting in, or exiting the pit lane. Pit-lane procedure is PS even when the car is accelerating out and returning toward the racing surface.
  - Require available pit evidence: `Graphics_is_in_pit` or a `locate_circuit_section` result that overlaps the circuit's known pit entry, pit lane, or pit-exit corridor.
  - Do not label PS from speed rise, low speed, trajectory offset, or acceleration back toward track speed alone when the range is in a normal racing section away from pit entry/exit.
  - Use PS1 for the pit-exit phase specifically.
Compatible with the circuit label only; do NOT combine with EA / MSP / MSR / RM / O / OD.

O.name: Successful Overtake
O.characteristics:
Player gained a position on a specific opponent inside the section. Multi-car positional data (`Car_{1..60}_pos_{x,y,z}`) is the gate.
  - Call `classify_opponent_interaction(start, end)`. Require
    `outcome: pass_completed`, `gates.O: true`, and `label_gates.O: true` —
    the deterministic signed longitudinal relationship says the opponent
    was ahead at entry and behind by exit. Empty / no-data / non-pass
    outcomes ⇒ do NOT attach O. Low / weak confidence means inspect opponent
    trajectory or submit an empty label list.
  - Player-trace evidence to ALSO hold: late-brake signature
    past the expert reference, sustained outside / inside line
    deviation NOT explained by MSP / RM, or speed > expert on
    equal-or-less throttle (draft).
A close opponent + failed attack is MSR at the section level — sub-labelled `MSR1` in the detailed flow. A successful defense is OD, not O.

OD.name: Successful Defense
OD.characteristics:
Player held position against a real, close opponent inside the section.
  - Call `classify_opponent_interaction(start, end)`. Require
    `outcome: held_defense`, `gates.OD: true`, and `label_gates.OD: true` —
    the deterministic relationship says the opponent threatened from behind
    / alongside but did not get ahead by exit. A merely close car with no
    held-defense outcome is not OD. Low / weak confidence means inspect opponent
    trajectory or submit an empty label list.
  - Player-trace evidence to ALSO hold: brake initiation
    earlier than expert and/or trajectory tighter than expert
    (inside cover), or a throttle lift on a straight with no
    brake onset (defensive lift). Time delta need not be flat
    — it may grow briefly during the defense as long as the
    position holds.
A defense that failed (opponent got past) is MSR at the section level — sub-labelled `MSR2` in the detailed flow.

practice: Solo sessions are processed as normal driving sections split by circuit section.
Only practice-session behavior parents {PS, RM, MSP} are eligible. Do not evaluate or attach racing-session behavior parents O / OD / MSR in practice mode.

Pick MSP for a technical driving mistake, RM for recovery from a prior mistake, or PS for pit-lane procedure. For MSP vs RM, classify by how the split section starts: starts with a mistake action => MSP even if recovery/merge happens later; starts with no new mistake and later recovers/merges from a carried prior issue => RM.
Use `find_trend_runs` and `compute_slope` on `expert_time_difference` for label-significant time-loss / recovery evidence. A constant carried gap is not a new mistake or recovery.
Use `find_extremum` on `trajectory_offset` for peak deviation plus returned near-zero summary (`near_zero_fraction`, `starts_near_zero`, `ends_near_zero`, `moves_toward_zero`).
Driver/expert turning / trajectory, brake, and throttle comparison is required for segment completeness at entry or exit, not only for sub-labels.
racing: Sessions with opponent data are processed only as close overtake offence / defense engagement windows.
Only racing-session behavior parents {O, OD, MSR, PS} are eligible. Do not evaluate or attach practice-session behavior parents MSP / RM in racing mode.
Pick O for a successful attacking pass, OD for a held defense, or MSR for a failed attack / broken defense.

The deterministic gate for O / OD / MSR is `classify_opponent_interaction(start, end)` over the full current range: O requires `outcome: pass_completed`; OD requires `outcome: held_defense`; MSR requires `outcome` in {`failed_attack`, `broken_defense`}.

Prefer labels only when the matching confidence-aware `label_gates` value is true. Low / weak classifier confidence means inspect `query_opponent_trajectory` or submit an empty label list if evidence remains unclear.

The classifier uses expert-trajectory projection for signed longitudinal / lateral gaps when expert positions exist, and reports `coordinate_frame` so cite whether it used `expert_path_projection` or `player_heading_projection`.
If the classifier does not support a required O / OD / MSR outcome, submit an empty label list rather than labeling normal practice-driving telemetry.
PS remains eligible in racing mode only for pit-lane procedure with pit evidence; do not use it for ordinary opponent interactions or combine it with O / OD / MSR.
Use `find_nearest_opponent` and `query_opponent_trajectory(start, end, slot, n_samples)` for supporting primary-slot details and technique.
common: Every saved lap segment must include at least one eligible behavior parent label. Circuit labels, circuit_section labels, segment-type labels, sub-labels, and EA do not satisfy this requirement.
If no eligible behavior parent fits the whole split-section range, submit `label_ids: []` to drop the range; do not save a segment with only circuit / section / segment-type / sub-label / EA labels.
Call `get_circuit_id` and `locate_circuit_section` for circuit context. Include circuit / circuit_section ids only when an eligible behavior parent is also included.
When `locate_circuit_section` reports `is_ambiguous`, disambiguate from `top_matches` with a second signal (persistent lateral offset, brake pattern, or speed trace) rather than guessing.

Whole-range label rule: every behavior, segment-type, and sub-label must describe the final annotation range as a whole. Do not attach a label because it matches only one phase, one apex moment, or a short slice inside the range; omit that label or leave it for detailed child sub-segment annotation.

Segment model: a saved lap parent segment is a group of one or more complete driving actions that together justify the behavior parent label over the final iloc range; it is not an arbitrary graph slice, a single apex moment, or one isolated label symptom.

Action model: each action must be evaluated as the related turning / trajectory, throttle input, and brake input over the same iloc interval. Zero or steady throttle / brake still count as input states when they explain the action.

Segment completeness rule: the parent segment must keep the complete action group needed for the chosen behavior parent. Do not clip the turning, throttle, or brake portion that makes the action understandable.

For entry actions, include the relevant turn-in / entry trajectory plus the complete brake action made by the driver and the comparable expert brake action: first relevant application / onset before turn-in through brake release / end of braking or the stable post-brake transition.

For exit actions, include the relevant exit / unwind trajectory plus the complete throttle action made by the driver and the comparable expert throttle action: first relevant reapplication or lift point through the stabilized exit / full-throttle state.

Before scoring the final parent label, identify the complete action or action group inside the proposed parent segment and cite the turning / trajectory, throttle, and brake evidence that makes it complete.

Bounds must come from these knowledge-base rules plus deterministic tool results over `Physics_brake` / `Physics_gas` and `expert_optimal_brake` / `expert_optimal_throttle`; do not substitute remembered conventions, graph-only guesses, or arbitrary padding.
If deterministic results do not establish the full action interval inside the split-section range, submit `label_ids: []` rather than saving an incomplete parent segment.
Render diagnostic graphs needed for the eligible labels. Use `trajectory_offset`, `expert_time_difference`, brake / throttle / speed, and deterministic telemetry queries as evidence.
Use `find_trend_runs` on `expert_time_difference` and cite returned `verdict`, `significant_runs`, `strongest_losing_time_run`, and `strongest_recovery_run` to localize gap growth or shrinkage.

Use `compute_slope` on `expert_time_difference` and cite returned `unit`, `delta_value`, `total_change_direction`, `total_change_significance`, `total_change_is_label_significant`, `end_change_direction`, and `end_trend_change` only as the whole-range summary after checking local trend runs.

Never invent math adjectives from the raw slope number; deterministic tool verdict fields are the source of truth for units, trend significance, local time-loss/recovery runs, end-window trend direction, and parent-segment action bounds.

If the picked main label, segment-type label, or sub-label fits only part of the split-section range, the engagement starts before the range, the pass resolves after the range, an entry brake action or exit throttle action would be clipped, or classifier confidence is low / weak, omit that label or submit `label_ids: []`.
Optionally pick segment-type labels when the base segment shape or corner-shape refinement is unambiguous and the returned catalog metadata has `lap_parent_allowed: true`.

Use `measure_segment_shape` as the deterministic segment-shape summary. Add a corner-shape refinement only when `measure_segment_shape.corner_shape_refinement.shape_key` matches that label's `deterministic_gate.required_shape_key` for the final range; non-empty `phases` alone is not enough.
ST10 Hairpin requires `measure_segment_shape.corner_shape_refinement` to report the required hairpin gate flag true: `is_near_u_turn`.

Entry/apex/exit altitude labels have `annotation_scope: subsegment_only` and `lap_parent_allowed: false`; they describe separate corner-phase subsegments, not a single lap parent segment covering the whole corner.

Submit `label_ids` plus a 4-6 sentence `reasoning` note citing deterministic verdict fields plus ilocs / values / offset peaks / classifier outcome / confidence level / opponent slot fields, as applicable.
Never invent label IDs. Use only IDs from the eligible behavior list, circuit / section capability results, or label catalog search results.
Empty `label_ids` `[]` is the valid drop-this-section signal, not a saved annotation without a required behavior parent.
Final iloc range is the split-section range and must be at least 3 ilocs.

global_rules: Compatibility note: session-specific lap detection policy lives in `lap_annotation.global_rules_by_session.practice`, `lap_annotation.global_rules_by_session.racing`, and `lap_annotation.global_rules_by_session.common`. Render the detected session mode plus common rules instead of this legacy key.
